note: Adapted from the species description of Ibitermes inflatus by Vasconcellos (2002), originally in English; the alate is unknown (recorded as Imago unknown in the original), hence only the soldier and worker are included; figure numbers, localities and biological records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier nasus distinctly extends beyond the apices of the mandibles, and the head capsule has strongly convex sides and an inflated middle, distinguishing the species from the other Ibitermes species. It is larger than I. tellustris and smaller than I. curupira. In the soldier of I. curupira the pronotum bears fewer setae on the anterior margin and surface, and the sides of the head are only weakly convex; in the soldier of I. tellustris the postclypeus is not inflated, the head has more setae, and the sides of the head are nearly parallel.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellow to yellowish brown; antennal segments 1 and 2 yellow, the remaining segments yellowish brown; postclypeus pale brown; postmentum and labrum yellow; base of the nasus and mandibles yellowish brown, the middle of the nasus brown, the apex sepia brown; pronotum yellowish white; remainder of the body white. Head with few setae. Postclypeus with 4 setae, 2 apical and 1 on each side. Pronotum with 10–14 setae on the anterior margin, 3–6 on the posterior margin and 25–30 on the surface. Meso- and metanota with setae on the posterior margins. Abdominal tergites and sternites with setae on the anterior and posterior margins, the surface densely hairy, most hairs directed posteriorly. Head capsule slightly elongate, the sides convex and the middle slightly inflated, the posterior margin slightly convex; nasus conical, its apex distinctly extending beyond the apices of the mandibles, slightly upturned in lateral view; postclypeus very strongly inflated, reaching the middle of the nasus in dorsal view, with a distinct median depression; labrum directed downward, concealed by the postclypeus in dorsal view; postmentum moderately elongate, the sides convex; mandibles stout, without marginal teeth, curved inward and downward; antennae 14-segmented, segment 2 longer than segments 3, 4 and 5, the last three nearly equal in length; anterior margin of the pronotum concave in the middle, the posterior margin slightly convex in the middle. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Fore coxa without a lateral process. Measurements: head length (to the apex of the nasus) 2.66–2.88 mm; nasus length 0.91–1.08 mm; head length (to the mandibular base) 1.65–1.79 mm; head width 1.50–1.67 mm; head height 1.16–1.23 mm; pronotum width 0.94–1.02 mm; hind tibia length 1.25–1.35 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Apparently monomorphic. Head and antennae yellowish white; thorax white; abdominal sclerites transparent, the gut contents visible. Posterior and lateral parts of the head with about 7–10 setae, around the fontanelle 6–15 short hairs. Postclypeus with about 4 setae, 2 on the anterior margin and 2 in the middle, together with a few hairs. Pronotum with 2–4 setae on the anterior margin and 2–4 on the posterior margin, the surface with scattered short to long hairs. Meso- and metanota with long hairs to setae on the posterior margins. Abdominal chaetotaxy as in the soldier. Postclypeus strongly inflated. Left mandible index 1.1. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 2 longer than segments 3 and 4; in some specimens segment 3 partly divided. Abdomen oval; the mesenteric band of the mixed segment arises from the dorsal side of the midgut arch and then twists, its distal end terminating on the ventral and posterior sides of the mixed segment.
